desc:
Consider every contiguous subarray of nums whose length is at least k. The median of a subarray of length len is the element at zero-based position len // 2 of its sorted copy (the larger middle value for an even length).

Return the largest median over all these subarrays.

nums = [3, 1, 4, 1, 5], k = 3
[3,1,4] -> 3     [1,4,1] -> 1     [4,1,5] -> 4
[3,1,4,1] -> 3   [1,4,1,5] -> 4   [3,1,4,1,5] -> 3
answer = 4
hints: Checking every subarray and sorting it is far too slow. Is the statement 'some valid subarray has median at least m' monotone in m?
For a fixed m, map each element to +1 if it is at least m and to -1 otherwise. The median of a subarray is at least m exactly when the mapped sum is non-negative.

Binary search the answer over the sorted values. For each candidate use prefix sums: for the end position j, you need some start i with j - i ≥ k and prefix[j] - prefix[i] ≥ 0, so keep the minimum prefix among allowed starts.
editorial: For a threshold m, let c be the number of subarray elements that are at least m and d the number below. The median (sorted position len // 2) is at least m exactly when at most len // 2 elements are below m, i.e. d ≤ len // 2, which is equivalent to c ≥ d, i.e. the +1/-1 sum is non-negative.

If a subarray works for m, it also works for every smaller value, so feasibility is monotone and the largest feasible m can be found by binary search over the sorted distinct array values (the answer is always one of them).

Each feasibility check is one pass: with prefix sums P, for each end j ≥ k maintain best = min(P[0..j-k]) and test P[j] - best ≥ 0. Total time is O(n log n) for sorting plus O(n log n) for the binary search.
